D1.name: Hiring Readiness Optimization

Plan 2 offers a broader list of project ideas without committing to one deployable capstone, leaving portfolio coherence to the user. Plan 1 integrates interview prep (DSA, behavioral STAR, system design) consistently across all four months, while Plan 2 concentrates interview prep almost entirely in Week 16. Plan 1's technical stack (Django, DRF, AWS, Docker, GitHub Actions) is more directly aligned with Cybersecurity Engineer SWE roles than Plan 2's broader but shallower coverage. Plan 2 does include valuable elements like CTF practice and PortSwigger labs that Plan 1 lacks, but these don't compensate for the weaker portfolio and delayed interview prep.
D1.winner_reason: Plan 1 delivers a single deployable, cloud-hosted capstone with CI/CD and security hardening, plus distributed interview prep — both critical for SWE hiring readiness.

D2.name: Time-Constrained Feasibility

Plan 2 never states total hours or a budget, making feasibility harder to verify. Plan 1's monthly hour breakdowns (43, 42, 42, 43) are consistent and realistic for 2 hours/day. However, Plan 1's Month 4 is extremely dense: Docker Compose, CI/CD with GitHub Actions, advanced cryptography, IDS/IPS, VPNs, offensive security tools (Nmap, ZAP, Burp Suite), and vulnerability reporting — all in one month. Plan 2's weekly structure is more modular and each week covers 2-3 topics, which is more cognitively manageable. Plan 2 also avoids some of the heavier engineering topics (full CI/CD pipeline, containerization) that strain the timeline, though this comes at the cost of portfolio depth.
D2.winner_reason: Plan 1's explicit hour budgeting and buffer allocation demonstrate superior time management discipline, despite Month 4 being slightly overloaded.
